industry: Athletic + work footwear (Merrell, Saucony, Sweaty Betty, Wolverine, Cat, Bates, Chaco, Harley-Davidson, HYTEST, Hush Puppies licensed)
drawdown_context: WWW entered the cutoff window at $16.43, down -32.2% from trailing 52-week high. Tape pressure reflects (i) post-divestiture revenue base reset (FY24 revenue $1,755M vs $2,243M FY23, -21.8%), (ii) macro tariff overhang on China-sourced footwear (100% sourced from third-party suppliers, predominantly Asia Pacific), and (iii) lingering distress associations from a multi-year transformation/de-leveraging that completed at year-end. The fundamentals BENEATH the drawdown actually inflected positive: FY24 returned to profitability ($47.9M net income vs $(39.6)M FY23 loss vs $(188.3)M FY22 loss), and Q1 2025 10-Q (filed May 8) confirmed +4.4% YoY revenue growth and a $0.13 EPS beat vs $(0.19) prior-year loss. This is a textbook cyclical drawdown on a name that has finished its restructuring, not a hidden distress event.

summary: WWW is a textbook honesty-alpha PASS: a footwear platform that just completed a 3-year transformation (Keds Feb 2023, Leathers H2 2023, Sperry Jan 2024, China JV Jan 2024, HushPuppies-NA license 2023, Merrell+Saucony kids license May 2024) and whose Q1 2025 10-Q -- filed 7 days before cutoff -- confirms the post-transformation inflection (revenue +4.4% YoY, gross margin 47.3%, net earnings $11.1M vs -$14.5M prior year). The covenant amendment cycle (Fifth Amendment Dec 2023) terminated 14+ months pre-cutoff and was DISPOSITION CAPACITY not COVENANT RELIEF; debt reduced -29.6% YoY ($921M -> $648M). The Ernst & Young 92-year auditor tenure is one of the longest in the S&P 1500, with clean ICFR. The $150M buyback authorization (March 2024) sits at $0 deployed through Q1 2025 -- the explicit OPPOSITE of the MGPI-style trough buyback defense pattern. The PFAS Rockford Tannery litigation accrual SHRINKS between the 10-K and the Q1 2025 10-Q ($39.7M -> $37.2M environmental, $10.1M -> $8.4M litigation) and the Plainfield Consent Decree is hard-capped at $69.5M. Zero 10b5-1 plan amendments across Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 rule out the insider-flight tell, and CEO Hufnagel (Wolverine lifer since 2013, former Merrell president) plus CFO Miller (in-seat 12+ months at cutoff) show no transition-around-bad-news pattern. The only Mode B yellow flag is the 3% Sweaty Betty cushion (explicitly elevated as the sole CAM by EY and re-tested at Q1 with no triggering event found) -- a single MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY entry. Composite should be in the deep PASS range (~0.12), validating the false-positive guardrail. The -32% drawdown is mispricing: external tariff overhang + post-divestiture revenue base reset on a name whose disclosure quality is uniformly anti-correlated with the distress patterns the framework looks for.
